# Positive Displacement Entry - By List

This functionality is only available for gas meters.

Use the PD Entry by List screen to quickly enter index readings for positive displacement and turbine meters from which FLOWCAL will calculate the net raw volume and distribute it evenly across the date range.

The previous removed (Off) information is used as the current placed (On) information.

<div class="example">

Tip - Keyboard Entry

The PD Entry by List screen is designed to be used with your keyboard's numeric key pad. You can type values into the grid and press the **Enter** key to navigate to the next cell. Real-time validations will occur when you follow this process. You can also navigate the grid using the mouse, but in this case, the data will not validate until you click the **Import** button.

</div>

 

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Entering Data">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Entering Data Manually</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Entering Data">

<div class="procedure">

To enter data in the PD Entry by List screen:

1.  Go to **Import** \> **Positive Displacement** \> **Entry by List**.

2.  Select a list, location, or individual meter.
    - If you select a meter that is not a positive displacement or turbine meter, a beep will sound and a message ("Not a turbine or displacement meter") will display at the bottom of the screen.
    - If you select a list or location, all of the positive displacement meters and turbine meters that you have access to will display in the grid.

3.  By default, meter/location numbers are used in the drop-down and on the grid. Click the **Use Names** checkbox beneath the grid to display meter/location names instead of numbers.

4.  After selecting your meter/location number, press **Tab** to navigate to the first empty grid cell to enter your data. If no data exists for the meter, the first empty cell will be **On Date**. If there is existing data for the meter, the first empty cell will be **Off Date**.

5.  The difference between the on and off readings is automatically calculated. Rollover values are handled by the calculations.

    By default, the reading values and the difference are stored as pulses. To store the readings and differences as raw volume, select that option in **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Default Values**.

6.  FLOWCAL provides the ability to set default pressures and temperatures. You can specify these values in **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Default Values**. If these values are set up, the grid will display them for new entries. You may overwrite them with updated values or skip over them as desired. If these value are not set up, the grid fields will be empty and you must provide the values.

7.  The resolution (Daily, Hourly, or As Is) will display based on the meter's characteristic data resolution for the specified time frame.

    As Is resolution will write one record for the specified time frame. Daily resolution will split the difference in readings across the appropriate number of days and write daily records for the specified time frame.

8.  When you press **Enter**, the data will validate and your cursor will navigate to the next row.

9.  If there are no more rows with meters, click **Import** or press **Enter** to import the data. Additional validations are performed on the data before writing it to the database. Any errors found during these validations will display on the Messages tab and written to the log file.

    To use this function, the Transaction Queue service must be installed and running.

    

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 597;height: 378;" />

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Parameters">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Data Entry Parameters</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Parameters">

| Field | Format Requirements |
|----|----|
| On Date/Off Date | 6 numeric digits (MMDDYY) |
| On Hour/Off Hour | 2 numeric digits (HH); use a leading 0 for single-digit hours |
| On Reading/Off Reading | Number of digits corresponds to the number of dials on the meter; this value is set in Meter Characteristics; if no value is specified, the default number is 6 |

If a value does not have the correct number of digits, the system will beep and a message will display in the status bar. The cursor will not advance, and the invalid data will be highlighted.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Read Tolerances">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Read Tolerances</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Read Tolerances">

Read tolerances (in days) may be set for monthly records on the **Meter Editor** \> **Reports** tab. Records with an actual (entered) on date within the read tolerance will be snapped to contract start of month. Records with an actual (entered) off date within the read tolerance will be snapped to the contract end of month.

PD Entry by List will not save:

- Long records with on or off dates outside the read tolerances.
- Records dated in the future. Both the on and off dates must occur before the date of entry. Off dates must occur after on dates.

</div>
